titulo: The loop in 5 pieces: goal, state, action, check, stop
lead: Every agent loop that works has the same five pieces, from /goal to the shell loop. When a loop fails, almost always one is missing: it doesn't say where it wants to get, it forgets where it was, it approves itself, or it doesn't know when to stop. Here you learn to see the five and run a toy loop, with no model, that shows them.
objetivo: identify the 5 pieces in any agent loop and run a toy loop that stops on its own, by the test or by the cap.

aprende.t: The five pieces and the question each one answers
Which piece is missing when the loop spins aimlessly or stops early
A toy loop in bash that stops on the test or the cap
Where each piece is explored in depth across the six courses

hero_alt: Braided black cable running through five different metal clips on a dark surface.

secoes.titulo: The five pieces of every loop
secoes.sub: Tap each block: the question the piece answers and what happens when it is missing.

nos.sub: where I want to end up

itens.t: A final state you can check

nos.detalhe: One sentence with an end you can check: a file with 5 lines, a test suite passing, an empty queue. Without it the loop has no way to know it is done, and it stops when the quota runs out or when the model decides it looks good enough.

itens.t: Lives in a file and in git
Without it: redoes or skips work

nos.detalhe: What has been done, what is left, and how to resume. In a long loop the model's context gets compacted, reset, or moved to a new session; whatever lives only in the conversation is lost. That is why the state lives outside the model (lesson 5).
What the agent does in this cycle: edit a file, run a command, ask for a tool. A small step is a verifiable step; five changes at once don't tell you which one broke.

itens.t: A command with an expected output
Without it: the agent approves itself

nos.detalhe: What says the step worked is a command, not the agent's opinion: the test runs and prints "6 passed", wc counts 5 lines. It is the piece that is missing most often and costs the most when it is missing. The 0–4 scale is in lesson 6; how to build the evaluator, in course 1.

Two exits, always: the good one (the goal was verified) and the safety one (a cap was hit or it stopped making progress). A loop without a cap is the one that spins all night on the same broken test. The five caps are in lesson 7.

secoes.volta: Not done and no cap hit? Reread the state and start another cycle.
secoes.legenda: It applies to a shell loop, to Claude Code's /goal, to codex exec inside a script, and to the nine LOOP-R agents.

rolagem_fim.texto: Where do I want to end up? Where am I? What is the next step? Did it work, with proof? Do I stop or continue? A loop that answers all five with a file and a command works on its own; one that answers with the model's memory depends on luck.

secoes.sub: Four symptoms everyone has seen, and the piece that fixes each.

texto: The agent finishes with a confident summary and the test never ran. The goal existed, but nobody checked it.
Fix: the stop depends on a command that prints the result, and the proof shows up in the output.

exemplo.texto: "leave the tests passing" → "python3 -m pytest -q prints 6 passed"

texto: The same broken test, the same attempt, cycle after cycle, until the quota runs out.
Fix: a cap on cycles and a stagnation rule, for example 3 cycles without measured progress = stop and call you.
After a compaction or a new session, the agent restarts a finished item or skips a pending one.
Fix: the state goes to a file and to git, and every cycle starts by rereading it (lesson 5).
"Improve the code" has no end: each cycle finds one more thing.
Fix: an end state you can check with a command. If you can't write the command, the task isn't ready to become a loop yet.

secoes.titulo: The five pieces in 15 lines of bash
secoes.sub: No model at all: the "action" is one line of shell. The goal is to see the pieces, not the agent.

blocos.conteudo:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Toy loop: the 5 pieces with no model at all. The "agent" is one line of shell.
set -u
OBJETIVO=5                         # 1. goal: saida.txt with 5 lines
ESTADO=estado.txt                  # 2. state: lives in a file, not in memory
MAX_CICLOS=8                       # 5. stop: cap on cycles
touch saida.txt
ciclo=$(cat "$ESTADO" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
while true; do
  feitas=$(wc -l < saida.txt)      # 4. check: one command, before acting
  echo "ciclo $ciclo: $feitas de $OBJETIVO linhas"
  if [ "$feitas" -ge "$OBJETIVO" ]; then echo "PRONTO no ciclo $ciclo"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$ciclo" -ge "$MAX_CICLOS" ]; then echo "PARADO: teto de $MAX_CICLOS ciclos"; exit 2; fi
  ciclo=$((ciclo + 1)); echo "$ciclo" > "$ESTADO"
  echo "item $ciclo" >> saida.txt  # 3. action
done

blocos.rot: Terminal · run in an empty folder
blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p ~/ensaio-loop/pecas && cd ~/ensaio-loop/pecas
# paste the script above into loop-brinquedo.sh and run:
bash loop-brinquedo.sh; echo "rc=$?"
bash loop-brinquedo.sh; echo "rc=$?"   # again: it's already done, so it doesn't act

abas.html:
$ bash loop-brinquedo.sh; echo "rc=$?"
ciclo 0: 0 de 5 linhas
ciclo 1: 1 de 5 linhas
ciclo 2: 2 de 5 linhas
ciclo 3: 3 de 5 linhas
ciclo 4: 4 de 5 linhas
ciclo 5: 5 de 5 linhas
PRONTO no ciclo 5
rc=0

$ bash loop-brinquedo.sh; echo "rc=$?"
ciclo 5: 5 de 5 linhas
PRONTO no ciclo 5
rc=0

The second run adds nothing: the state is in the file and the check comes before the action.

$ bash loop-brinquedo.sh | tail -3; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
ciclo 7: 7 de 20 linhas
ciclo 8: 8 de 20 linhas
PARADO: teto de 8 ciclos
rc=2

The goal doesn't fit under the cap: the loop exits through the safety door, with a nonzero code, instead of spinning forever.

secoes.titulo: Where each piece is explored in depth
paragrafos: This course gives the anatomy; the other five go deeper into one piece each. Verification: course 1 (separate evaluator, frozen tests, reward hacking). State and goal in a run that lasts hours: course 2 (the seven-file kit and the goal.md).
Action split across several agents: course 3. Limits on what the agent can do: course 4. And the loop that improves its own process, with promotion and rollback: course 5.

secoes.sub: On your machine. Only move on to the next one when the "done when" is true.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · The toy loop stops on the check
exercicios.texto: Create ~/ensaio-loop/pecas, paste in loop-brinquedo.sh and run it twice in a row.
exercicios.pronto: The first run ends with PRONTO no ciclo 5 and rc=0; the second prints only ciclo 5: 5 de 5 linhas and PRONTO no ciclo 5, and wc -l < saida.txt → 5.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · The loop stops on the cap
exercicios.texto: Delete saida.txt and estado.txt, change OBJETIVO=5 to OBJETIVO=20 and run it again.
exercicios.pronto: The last line is PARADO: teto de 8 ciclos and echo $? right after → 2.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Diagnosis of a loop of your own
exercicios.texto: Take the last long request you made to Claude Code or Codex. In a file named pecas.md, write one line per piece, starting with objetivo:, estado:, ação:, verificação: and parada:, saying what filled that role, or faltou. Write the markers exactly like this, in Portuguese: the "done when" grep looks for them.
exercicios.pronto: grep -ciE '^(objetivo|estado|ação|verificação|parada):' pecas.md → 5, and at least one line says "faltou" or points to a real command.

perguntas.p: The agent finished by saying "I implemented it and everything works," but no test shows up in the output. Which piece was missing?
perguntas.explica: There was a goal and an action; what was missing was a command that proved it. Without a check, the agent's opinion decides when it's done. The common mistake is to blame the goal: it may be clear and still nobody checked.

perguntas.p: In the toy loop, why doesn't the second run add the 6th line?
opcoes: Because bash remembers the previous run
Because the check runs before the action and the state is in a file
Because saida.txt is deleted at the start
perguntas.explica: The script rereads estado.txt and saida.txt, checks first and only acts if something is missing. The bash process keeps nothing between runs: the memory is the file. If the check came after the action, the second run would write one extra line before noticing.

perguntas.p: A loop has a verifiable goal, state in a file and a test per cycle, but no cap. What can go wrong?
opcoes: Nothing: if the test is good, it always finishes
It can spin indefinitely when the goal is impossible or the agent gets stuck
perguntas.explica: A good test guarantees it doesn't exit too early, not that it exits. An impossible goal or an agent stuck on the same error only stops at a cap: cycles, time, memory, stagnation or cost.

perguntas.p: Which goal is ready to become a loop?
opcoes: Improve the quality of the login module
python3 -m pytest -q tests/auth prints 0 failed and the number of tests does not decrease
perguntas.explica: It's the only one with an end that a command can check. The others never finish or depend on opinion. The full scale, with what makes a criterion shortcut-proof, is in lesson 6.

itens.texto: Goal, state, action, verification and stop: every loop that works has all five.
What decides that a step worked is a command's output; what decides to stop is the test or a cap.
Done by verification or stopped by the cap, with a different exit code for each.
